title: 'For Argument's Sake, Show Me How to Harm Myself!': Jailbreaking LLMs in Suicide and Self-Harm Contexts
identity_check: Opens with the arXiv:2507.02990 title ''For Argument's Sake, Show Me How to Harm Myself!': Jailbreaking LLMs in Suicide and Self-Harm Contexts', matching the assignment.
mapping_note: paper's 'safety protocols / guardrails / safety feature' that suppress harmful output -> our K2 inhibition-gate (MAPPING: 'gate' is ours); paper's 'trigger the safety protocols' and 'introduction of another context ... to override the safety function' -> our K1 trigger/threshold ('trigger' is the authors' word).
description_scope: Judged under 'supplying self-harm/suicide methods = the action, refusal = withholding'; whether the gate holds depends on the description the user applies (self-directed intent vs academic/hypothetical argument).
motion_source: L4 - conversational framing and perceived user intent (pragmatic layer) move the safety filter; no representation-level carrier is examined.

mechanism.claim: A safety guardrail acts as an intent-gated filter that, when engaged, withholds self-harm/suicide methods and redirects to help-seeking.
mechanism.quote: this model refuses to provide information in both test cases, mimics empathy, and provides contacts for help-seeking

mechanism.claim: Reframing the identical harmful query under a new context (e.g. an academic argument) is the trigger that reliably defeats the safety filter within a couple of turns.
mechanism.quote: we can bypass safety mechanisms reliably by changing the context and perceived intent of the prompt

event_grammar: [MOTION] self-disclosed harmful intent is presented --> [GATE] safety protocol gates method-providing (refusal) --> [ACTION/INACTION] reframed as academic argument opens the gate => harmful content emitted (action); otherwise withheld (inaction) --> [OUTCOME] safety-protocol failure across several commercial LLMs --> [FEEDBACK] the gate flips within ~2 conversation turns on a context switch

anchor_concordance.reason: SUPPORTS the single-direction claim only at the behavioural/gate level (a defeasible refusal gate that adversarial context switches off, exactly what the anchor's adversarial-suffix result predicts); N2 never inspects internal activations, so it neither confirms nor refutes the 'single direction' specificity and does not argue refusal is representationally distributed.

notes: Purely behavioural prompt-level study of 6 commercial LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Pi); no activation/steering analysis, so it bears no evidence on the representational count of directions. Cites the anchor in references. Authors' own limitation: no rigorous quantitative threshold for declaring a 'protocol failure'.
layers_provenance: L01-D5: the protocol's §2 field list requires layers[], but the coding schema dropped it and l01_gate.py's field loop did not check it. Recovered by extracting exactly the L-tokens already present in motion_source, in first-mention order - no layer is invented here
